title: Temperature
about: Turn one setting to make a chatbot more predictable or more surprising.

cards.prompt: Chatbots have a setting called **temperature**. Slide it and watch the chances change. Move it until **mat** has a chance of at least **80%**.
cards.hint: Try sliding both ways and watch the bar for "mat". Which way makes it grow?
cards.nudge: That way spreads the chances out. Try the other way.
cards.explanation: A **low** temperature makes the likeliest word even likelier. Turn it right down and it's "mat" almost every time: predictable.

cards.title: Turning the dial
cards.body:
**Temperature** changes how the model uses its chances.

- **Low:** the likeliest word gets even likelier. Predictable.
- **1:** the chances stay as learned.
- **High:** the chances even out. Surprising, sometimes nonsense.

The top word always stays on top. When one word has nearly all the chance, even a fairly high temperature usually picks it.

cards.prompt: Now make the model more surprising: move the temperature until **no word** has more than a **45%** chance.
cards.hint: The top word is the one to bring down. Which way evens the chances out?
cards.nudge: "mat" still has too big a share. Keep going in the same direction, further than feels normal.
cards.explanation: Only a **high** temperature brings "mat" below 45%. Press "Generate 5": at this setting the cat sometimes sits on the moon. Bold choice. More surprising, and more likely to be nonsense.

cards.prompt: At temperature 1, "mat" has a 60% chance. You turn the temperature right **down** and the model carries on from "The cat sat on the" **10** times. What happens?

options.text: It picks "mat" about 6 times out of 10
options.nudge: That's what happens at temperature 1. What does a very low temperature do to the top word?

options.text: It picks a different word each time
options.nudge: That's closer to what a very high temperature does.
Low temperature helps the top word, it doesn't hide it.

cards.hint: What does a very low temperature do to the top word's chance?
cards.explanation: A very low temperature makes the top word's chance shoot up, so it picks "mat" **almost every time**. About 6 out of 10 is what you'd expect at temperature 1.

cards.prompt: Same chatbot, same temperature. Ask it for a story idea twice and you get two different ideas. Ask it "What's 2 + 2?" twice and you get 4 both times. Why?

options.text: It's almost sure of "4", but many story ideas have similar chances
It remembers its first story idea and tries not to repeat itself
options.nudge: Each time, it just works out chances and picks. Think about how sure it is in each case.

options.text: Stories are harder, so it keeps getting them wrong and trying again
options.nudge: A story idea can't really be wrong. Compare how many good next words each question has.

options.text: Sums use a different, stricter temperature than stories do
options.nudge: The prompt says the temperature is the same. So the difference must be in the chances themselves.

cards.hint: Imagine the chances for each one. Is there one clear winner, or lots of close ones?
cards.explanation: When one word has nearly all the chance, like "4", it gets picked every time. When lots of words have similar chances, like story ideas, the picks vary. Temperature decides how much that variety shows.

cards.prompt: Jobs with **one right answer** want the most likely word every time. Jobs where you want **variety** can use a higher temperature. Sort each job.
cards.hint: For each job, ask: is there one right answer, or do you want lots of different ideas?
cards.nudge: Jobs with one right answer want the most likely answer every time. Which ones are like that?
cards.explanation: Maths, summaries and spelling have **one right answer**, so low is best. Band names, silly poems and story twists want **variety**, so a higher temperature helps. Most chatbot apps pick the temperature for you, but some tools let you change it.

cards.prompt: A small model's top word after "The capital of Australia is" is **Sydney**. (The real capital is Canberra.) You turn the temperature right down. What happens?

options.text: It switches to "Canberra", because a low temperature makes it more careful
options.nudge: Temperature never changes the order of the words. Which word is on top?

options.text: It says "Canberra" more often, because low temperature favours true answers
options.nudge: Low temperature favours the top word, whatever it is. Is the top word true here?

options.text: It says each city about equally, because the chances even out
options.nudge: Evening out is what a high temperature does. What does a low one do?

cards.hint: Low temperature makes the **top** word win. Which word is on top here, and is it true?
cards.explanation: A low temperature makes the top word win almost every time, and here the top word is wrong. Temperature changes **how** it picks, never **what it knows**: it can make a mistake more predictable, not fix it.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Temperature** changes how a model picks; the order never changes.
- Low: predictable, for one right answer. High: variety, then nonsense.
- It changes how it picks, never what it knows.

Next: why chatbots sometimes make things up.
